data.title: Two Trades To Watch: Gold, GBP/USD Forecast - Thursday, Nov. 19
data.description:
Gold tumbles to a fresh 14-month low on hawkish Fed rhetoric

Gold has fallen to a fresh 14-month low as hawkish Fed expectations have lifted the U.S. dollar to a 19-month high and pushed Treasury yields higher.

Minutes from the October FOMC meeting showed strong alignment among Fed officials on the need for further rate hikes. At the October meeting, the Fed left rates unchanged at 3.75% to 4% in a 10-to-2 vote, having hiked rates by 25 basis points in September.

The market is pricing in a 93% probability of a 25-basis-point hike next month and a 10% probability of a 50-basis-point hike. Three interest rate hikes are expected between now and March next year.

U.S. Treasury yields are rising, with the 10-year yield above 5% and flashing strong technical signals of a sustained upward move. The U.S. dollar has also risen to a 19-month high.

Together, these developments are taking the shine off non-yielding, dollar-denominated gold.

It will likely take the Federal Reserve adopting a more dovish stance towards the end of the hiking cycle for gold to recover.

Gold forecast – technical analysis

 XAU/USD has dropped to a 14-month low below $3,700. The price is trading in a descending channel and below both its 50 and 200 EMAs, keeping the technical picture bearish. The RSI is approaching oversold territory, although there are few signs of a reversal at this stage. Yesterday's decisive break below $3,800 has reinforced the bearish bias.

Sellers will look to break below support at $3,700, the 2026 low and the lower boundary of the falling channel. A sustained move below here would open the door towards $3,500, the round-number level and the 2025 high.

Should support at $3,700 hold, buyers would first need to reclaim $3,880, the October low and the midpoint of the descending channel. A break above here would bring the 50 EMA and July low at $3,960 into focus, followed by $4,150, the November high.

A rise above $4,150 creates a higher high and improves the technical outlook, bringing the 200 EMA at $4,230 into focus.

GBP/USD falls to a yearly low on USD strength and after cooler than forecast UK inflation data

GBP/USD is under pressure around the 1.3135 level, trading down 1.75% so far in November amid persistent U.S. dollar strength.

The U.S. dollar has extended its gains following hawkish Federal Reserve expectations. While the central bank left rates unchanged at the October meeting, following a 25-basis-point hike in September, the latest minutes saw officials express confidence in the need for further rate hikes to curb inflation.

The market is pricing in a 90% probability of a 25-basis-point hike in December and a 10% chance of a 50-basis-point hike. Three hikes are priced in between now and March.

Meanwhile, data this week showed that UK inflation rose by 3.6% year on year in October, up from 3.5% in September, but below expectations of 3.75%. Core inflation and services inflation, which the Bank of England watches closely, both defied expectations of a rise and held steady.

This suggests there is still little clear evidence of indirect effects from the energy shock passing through into core or services inflation. However, indirect effects could become more visible over time.

The Bank of England sees headline inflation reaching almost 5% by Q2 2027.

The market is pricing in around an 80% probability of a hike from the Bank of England in December, down from 90% ahead of the data. The market is also pricing in four rate hikes between now and the end of next year, which appears quite aggressive. Any unwinding of these expectations could pull GBP/USD lower.

GBP/USD forecast – technical analysis

GBP/USD has broken below the key 1.3200 support zone, dropping to 1.3120, a fresh yearly low. With the RSI below 50 but not yet in oversold territory, there is potential for further downside. 1.3100 is the next near-term target, ahead of 1.3150, the 2025 low.

Any recovery would need to regain the 1.3150–1.3200 zone and rise above 1.3300 resistance. This would help put the price on a slightly firmer footing before exposing the 50 EMA at 1.3330 and the 200 EMA at 1.3380. A rise above 1.3500 is needed to create a higher high.

data.title: Don't Overlook These Top-Rated Stocks After Q3 Earnings: ZIM, AS, BEKE
data.description:
Image: Bigstock

With valuation concerns still looming over Wall Street, investors are increasingly looking beyond expensive growth stocks for reasonably valued investment opportunities.

In particular, ZIM Integrated Shipping Services (ZIM - Free Report), Amer Sports (AS - Free Report), and KE Holdings (BEKE - Free Report) stand out after exceeding Q3 earnings expectations this week, offering an intriguing combination of reasonable valuations, improving profitability, and robust growth prospects.

ZIM Integrated Shipping Services – Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) | Stock Price: $29 | Forward P/E: 3X

Shipping stocks have been among this year's stronger performers, with the Zacks Transportation-Shipping Industry currently ranking in the top 10% of more than 240 Zacks industries.

ZIM remains one of the more attractively priced shipping stocks, trading under $30 a share and at less than 1X annual sales with a forward P/E of just 3X.

Further underscoring its attractive valuation, the container shipping giant reported stellar Q3 adjusted earnings of $5.94 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus of $4.77 by 24% and skyrocketing from EPS of $1.02 in the prior-year quarter. Quarterly revenue surged 53% to $2.71 billion, while adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $1.33 billion.

ZIM also raised its full-year guidance and declared a generous $2.01-per-share dividend, payable December 8 to shareholders of record as of November 30.

Adding to its appeal is the pending acquisition by Hapag-Lloyd at $35 a share, representing nearly 17% upside from Wednesday’s closing price of $29.92, although the deal remains subject to regulatory approvals.

Amer Sports – Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) | Stock Price: $30 | Forward P/E: 23X

Known for premium brands such as Arc'teryx, Salomon, and Wilson, Amer Sports continues to deliver impressive top-and bottom-line expansion.

Q3 revenue surged 23% to $2.16 billion, exceeding estimates of $2.12 billion, while adjusted earnings rose 27% to $0.42 per share, topping EPS expectations of $0.34 by 23%.

Strength was broad-based, with Technical Apparel revenue rising 26% and Outdoor Performance sales increasing 27%. Encouragingly, adjusted operating margin expanded by 70 basis points to 16.4%.

Amer Sports also raised its full-year revenue, margin, and earnings guidance while announcing a $1 billion share repurchase authorization.

Trading at $30 a share and at 23X forward earnings, AS stock offers a compelling growth profile, with high double-digit EPS growth expected in FY26 and FY27. Supporting this outlook, the Zacks Consensus calls for annual sales to increase 25% this year and another 17% in FY27 to $9.57 billion.

KE Holdings – Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) | Stock Price: $18 | Forward P/E: 15X

China-based real estate services platform KE Holdings is another affordable stock to consider, trading below $20 a share and at 15X forward earnings.

Despite challenges in China's property market, KE Holdings delivered Q3 adjusted EPS of $0.35, comfortably exceeding expectations of $0.25 and rising from $0.16 a year ago.

Although quarterly revenue was slightly down to $3.13 billion this still edged estimates of $3.06 billion and adjusted net income more than doubled to $389 million, highlighting improving operational efficiency.

Growth opportunities in home renovation and rental services, along with share repurchases, further support BEKE's investment appeal.

Bottom Line

With market volatility and valuation concerns lingering, these three stocks are worth considering following their strong Q3 results. ZIM, AS, and BEKE also sport an overall “A” VGM Zacks Style Scores grade, reflecting a favorable combination of Value, Growth, and Momentum, in addition to their attractive Zacks Ranks.

data.title: Disney Confirms More Layoffs After Revealing $392 Million In Severance Costs
data.description:
The Walt Disney Company's (DIS) cost-cutting efforts are far from over, even after multiple rounds of layoffs and a year of strong financial performance.

The entertainment giant has spent much of 2026 reorganizing its businesses, eliminating jobs and streamlining operations under new CEO Josh D’Amaro.

Now, fresh financial disclosures reveal just how expensive those changes have been.

Disney recorded $392 million in severance charges alone during fiscal 2026, including $212 million in its fourth quarter, according to its latest annual report.

And more job cuts are coming.

“We do expect more layoffs,” Disney Chief Financial Officer Hugh Johnston told CNBC following the company’s earnings announcement on Nov. 17.

The confirmation comes as Disney outlines an ambitious plan to generate approximately $3 billion in annual operating expense savings by fiscal 2029, even as it increases investments in its streaming, theme park, and cruise businesses.

Disney reveals $392 million severance bill as layoffs continue

Disney’s latest SEC filing shows that restructuring and impairment charges together reached approximately $1.46 billion in fiscal 2026, up from $819 million a year earlier.

Not all of those expenses were directly related to workforce reductions. The total included $1.01 billion in investment impairments, primarily associated with A+E Global Media, and $52 million in other restructuring costs.

But the severance bill alone was substantial.

The company disclosed:

  • Entertainment: $256 million in severance charges

  • Experiences: $29 million in severance charges

  • Sports: $87 million in restructuring expenses associated with severance and exiting a facility

The Sports figure includes facility-related expenses and does not represent severance alone.

The latest disclosures follow months of workforce reductions across Disney’s businesses.

As I previously reported, the company eliminated more than 1,500 positions across three rounds of layoffs between April and September. Additional cuts followed in October within Disney Experiences, including positions at Walt Disney Imagineering in California.

Earlier this month, Bloomberg reported that Disney managers had been asked to identify potential cost savings of up to 20% in certain departments, putting thousands more jobs at risk.

Disney has not disclosed how many additional employees will lose their jobs or when the next reductions will take place.

During the Nov. 17 earnings call, D’Amaro acknowledged the human impact of the restructuring.

“Changes like these are not easy, and they affect people who care deeply about Disney and have contributed so much to this company,” he said.

D’Amaro argued that these difficult decisions are necessary for Disney to operate faster and continue investing in the businesses driving its growth.

Disney outlines where $3 billion in savings will come from

Disney’s new efficiency program extends well beyond workforce reductions.

During the earnings call, Johnston identified procurement, sourcing, information technology, real estate consolidation, and shared services as areas where the company expects to reduce operating expenses.

Disney is also targeting selling, general, and administrative costs across its operating divisions and corporate functions.

“We are laser-focused on productivity and efficiency,” Johnston told analysts.

“We are all about delivering the short term and investing in the long term, not an either/or,” he said.

Most of the approximately $3 billion in annual savings will be reinvested in the company, primarily to support streaming and other direct-to-consumer services through content, technology, and marketing. A portion will also contribute directly to profitability.

Disney is also increasingly using artificial intelligence to improve efficiency.

During the call, D’Amaro said technology developed by Disney Research Studios and Industrial Light & Magic can reduce computing requirements for rendering films by approximately 30%.

“AI helps us work faster across the company,” he said.

The company is also using AI to improve design planning and operations at its theme parks.

However, Disney has not directly connected these AI initiatives to specific layoffs.

The strategy reflects what management calls its “One Disney” approach, which seeks to bring previously separate operations closer together.

Disney has already consolidated marketing and brand leadership, appointed its first chief technology officer and shifted consumer products closer to its entertainment business.

In a Nov. 17 research report shared with TheStreet, titled “Striking the right balance of growth and investment,” UBS analysts said the efficiency program should give Disney greater capacity to reinvest in streaming and Experiences while supporting profit growth.

UBS maintained its Buy rating and $133 price target, noting that Disney remains positioned for double-digit underlying earnings growth in fiscal 2027.

The bank also highlighted the company’s ability to balance investment in theme parks, cruises, and streaming with profitability improvements.

That balance is becoming increasingly important as Disney pursues aggressive expansion while continuing to reduce operating costs.

Disney+ and Hulu are coming together in December

Disney is also approaching another significant milestone in its efforts to combine businesses and streamline operations.

During the Nov. 17 earnings call, D’Amaro confirmed that Disney+ and Hulu will move to a fully unified experience beginning in December 2026.

“Disney+ and Hulu, they are coming together in one app,” D’Amaro said.

He clarified that Disney is not launching an entirely new app. Instead, the company is building on the existing Disney+ platform, with additional features expected to arrive beginning in spring 2027.

The December integration will also introduce more live sports, podcasts, and other programming, although access to certain content and add-ons will depend on subscribers’ plans.

The company has not announced that Hulu’s separate app will shut down in December.

As TheStreet reported, the integration is part of a broader strategy to make Disney+ a central destination for entertainment and increase engagement among subscribers.

The changes come as Disney continues restructuring its traditional television businesses around streaming.

The company has also been considering organizational changes affecting ABC Entertainment, Hulu Originals, 20th Television, and Freeform, as TheStreet previously reported.

Disney has not said whether the December integration will lead to further workforce reductions. But with its $3 billion annual savings target extending through fiscal 2029 and management now confirming additional layoffs, the company’s restructuring efforts are clearly not finished.

What remains uncertain for employees is which divisions will face the next reductions and how extensive those cuts will be.

data.title: MetaComp Extends Pre-A+ with Approximately US$10M from Tether and Further
data.description:
Strategic extension to deepen MetaComp's Asia–Middle East–Africa payment corridors; proceeds will fund licensing, compliance and payment rails

SINGAPORE, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- MetaComp Pte. Ltd. ("MetaComp"), Asia's pioneer in Web2.5 stablecoin/fiat hybrid finance, today announced an extension of its Pre-A+ funding round, with a strategic investment of approximately US$10 million from Tether, the largest company in the digital asset industry, and Further Asset Management ("Further"). The extension brings MetaComp's Pre-A funding round to about US$45 million.

Deepening collaboration on Asia–Middle East–Africa corridors

Trade between Asia, the Middle East and Africa continues to grow, driving demand for faster and compliant cross-border payments. MetaComp's hybrid fiat and stablecoin infrastructure reduces the intermediaries, settlement delays and fragmented networks that slow traditional cross-border payments on these corridors, reducing settlement from 2-7 days to within 24 hours. With an established client base in Asia, MetaComp supports businesses expanding into markets across Asia, the Middle East, Africa and Latin America, while serving financial institutions and businesses with cross-border payment, wealth management and loan capital raising needs in this region.

Further Asset Management ("Further") is an Abu Dhabi-based global investment platform focused on financial infrastructure and digital assets. Further brings sector expertise and institutional relationships to support MetaComp's growth, including its expansion in the Middle East.

Use of proceeds

The strategic investment from Tether and Further will accelerate MetaComp's expansion, with proceeds directed towards strengthening its regulatory capabilities, enhancing compliance infrastructure and developing additional payment channels across priority markets.

The extension builds on MetaComp's US$35 million Pre-A and Pre-A+ funding completed in March 2026, backed by investors including Alibaba, Eastern Bell Capital, Noah, Sky9 Capital, and Spark Venture.

Why investors back MetaComp

Licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) as a Major Payment Institution, MetaComp, together with its affiliates[1], provides one-stop financial services from cross-border payments to wealth management.

The platform connects with more than 60 financial institutions and more than 170 payment service providers (PSPs), serves more than 1,000 institutional clients, including leading companies across a wide range of industry verticals, supports 60 currencies across fiat and a range of stablecoins, and processes more than US$1 billion in monthly volume. Assets under management exceed US$600 million. [2]

MetaComp also operates the StableX Agentic Network (SAN), an agentic payment network leveraging stablecoins for AI agents to transact with each other, that is built on SAN's Know-Your-Agent (KYA) compliance standard for network admission and VisionX AI risk intelligence engine for transaction monitoring across fiat and on-chain activities. Since its launch in November 2025, the network has grown to more than 1,000 members reaching more than 100,000 users, with a primary focus on Asia, Middle East, Africa and Latin America.

Dr Bo Bai, Chairman and Co-Founder of MetaComp, said: "MetaComp has deep roots among companies from Asia, and our network has grown with them as they expand into other parts of Asia, the Middle East, Africa and Latin America. Trade between Asia and the Middle East and Africa is growing fast, and this extension, with Tether and Further, strengthens our capabilities along these corridors. We are building next-generation hybrid financial infrastructure that combines traditional banking rails with stablecoins, giving our clients integrated payment and wealth services in these regions as they expand overseas. The capital will be directed towards licences, compliance and payment channels, the foundations this infrastructure depends on."
Paolo Ardoino, Chief Executive Officer of Tether, said: "Trade between Asia, the Middle East and Africa is growing fast, but the money behind it still moves too slowly and at too high a cost. Regulated stablecoin infrastructure can change that, and these corridors are exactly where we see potential for USD₮ and XAU₮. Our investment in MetaComp reflects our focus on building that infrastructure in emerging markets, where faster and cheaper settlement matters most."
Faisal Al Hammadi, Managing Partner at Further Asset Management, said: "For stablecoins to become everyday financial infrastructure, businesses need reliable connections to the banking systems they already use. MetaComp brings together fiat and stablecoin payment rails, compliance technology and an established institutional client base. That combination fits our investment focus on the infrastructure enabling institutional adoption of digital assets. We look forward to supporting the team's growth and helping it build institutional partnerships across the Middle East."

[1] Wealth products and services are offered under the WealthX brand by MetaComp's affiliated licensed entities, each within the scope of its licence. All products and services relating to securities and capital markets products are offered and operated solely by Alpha Ladder Finance Pte. Ltd.

[2] Accurate as of 30 October 2026.

About MetaComp

MetaComp is a Singapore-headquartered payments company licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore as a Major Payment Institution. Guided by "Easier Payments, Resilient by Design," MetaComp connects fiat and stablecoin rails through a compliant Web2.5 architecture, enabling institutions and businesses to move, convert and manage capital seamlessly across borders.

MetaComp is advancing the next evolution of payments through the StableX Agentic Network, which has grown to more than 1,000 members reaching over 100,000 users. Through AgentX, AI agents can access MetaComp's regulated payment capabilities directly, supported by the StableX Know Your Agent (KYA) Framework, launched in April 2026, for agent governance, and VisionX for integrated fiat and on-chain compliance intelligence.

Learn more at www.mce.sg, or follow MetaComp on LinkedIn @metacompsg and X @MetaCompHQ.

About Further Asset Management

Further is a global investment platform connecting pioneering financial infrastructure with global capital markets. The firm provides institutional investors with access to regulated opportunities across venture, structured products, and digital assets. Its managed entities empower partners to execute sophisticated financial operations—from tokenization to seamless settlement—with security and precision. Chosen by founders and institutions from San Francisco to Hong Kong, Further is a strategic partner known for its focused capital, regulatory expertise, and ability to scale category-defining companies at the frontier of finance. To learn more, visit further.ae.

data.title: Lenovo Group Stock Analysis After Earnings: Is This Dell Rival A Buy Or Sell?
data.description:
Lenovo Group (LNVGY) stock remained under pressure on Thursday after the technology company published its financial results. It was trading at H$16.72, down by over 55% from its all-time high. Its technicals suggest that it has more downside in the near term. 

Lenovo Group’s business continued doing well

Lenovo Group, a leading competitor to Dell (DELL) and HP Enterprise (HPE), reported strong financial results for the latest quarter. The figures show the company’s business continued to grow, driven by ongoing investment in artificial intelligence (AI).

The results showed that its revenue growth gained momentum. Its revenue soared by 46% YoY to $30.2 billion, with its AI-related figure rising by 79. 

A look at its segments shows the business is thriving. The Intelligent Devices Group generated more than $17.4 billion in revenue, up 17% year on year, with an operating margin of 7.1%. This growth came as the company prioritized higher-priced devices, even as the number of units sold fell. 

Indeed, its premium PCs contributed to 63% of all PC shippings during the quarter. Recent data by Gartner (IT) showed that its PC sales dropped by 22.4% to 14.9 million during the quarter. Its PC margins have also dropped because of the ongoing memory shortage.

The Infrastructure Solutions Group’s revenue surged 178%, and its AI server pipeline reached $54 billion. 

Lenovo’s AI business is being driven by American hyperscalers, neoclouds, and Asian data center companies. Some of the revenue is coming from Asian data centers, especially in places like China and Malaysia. Lenovo’s Solutions and Services Group (SSG) grew by 205 to $3.1 billion. 

Still, the company made a $713 million loss during the quarter after losing over $1.19 billion in the same period last year. The loss was driven by fair value loss of $3.9 billion on derivative financial liabilities. 

Concerns about AI growth remains

Lenovo Group and other competitors have dropped in the past few months. For example, Dell stock has plunged by 46% from its highest point this year. It has dropped to its lowest level since May 28 this year.

HP Enterprise has also dropped to $45.78, down by 37% from the year-to-date high, while Super Micro Computer (SMCI) dropped by 52% in this period. Other companies in the AI space like Micron (MU), SanDisk, and Western Digital (WDC) have all plunged.

Investors are concerned about the potential slowdown in the coming months that would impact demand for its products. 

On the positive side, there are signs that demand is continuing to grow. For example, Nvidia (NVDA)’s earnings report showed that its revenue jumped to $115 billion in the third quarter, much higher than the expected $108 billion. 

Lenovo Group stock technical analysis

Lenovo Group stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that Lenovo Group’s stock has continued its strong sell-off in the past few months. It has slumped from $37 in September to the current $16.7. This retreat coincided with the ongoing weakness of other top companies in the AI space.

The stock has dropped below the 61.8% Fibonacci Retracement level of $19.73. In most cases, moving below that retracement normally confirms a bearish breakout. 

The stock has dropped below the 50-day and 200-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMA), and the two lines are about to cross each other. A crossover would lead to a death cross, a popular bearish outlook.

Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling, potentially to the key support level of $14.78, the 78.6% retracement level. A move below that level will point to more losses towards $10. In the future, however, there is a likelihood that the stock will bounce back, potentially to $20 and above.

data.title: Silver Investors Should Watch The Vaults, Not Just The Price
data.description:
Silver has slipped below $45 an ounce, yet the big vaults in London and New York have not been filling up, which means the fall is not coming from a surplus of metal, and the supply case for owning silver still stands.

If silver were piling up unsold, the big warehouses would usually show it. They do not. London held less silver at the end of October than a month earlier, the first fall in six months. In New York, the metal ready for delivery against futures barely moved while the price dropped. And India, the world's biggest silver consumer, spent nearly three times as much on silver imports in October as in September. On the stockpiles alone, that is a small positive for silver holders, based on one month of data. It is not a sign of a squeeze, and the next test starts on November 30.

Silver traded near $44.93 an ounce late on November 18. It was down about 5% on the day. Hawkish minutes from the Federal Reserve's last meeting added to bets on a December rate rise. The gold-silver ratio stood near 83, meaning one ounce of gold buys about 83 ounces of silver. Silver is now about 37% below its 2025 close. The latest premium issue at Golden Meadow® found the inventory picture calmer than the price.

There are six Deep Dives in this issue of the premium Silver Catalyst newsletter, and in this article, I'll focus on one of them.

 

London: The First Fall in Six Months

London is the centre of the world's wholesale silver trade, where large bars are stored. At the end of October its vaults held 28,889 tonnes, about 928.8 million ounces (Moz), according to the LBMA's monthly data. That is about 3.1 Moz less than at the end of September, after five monthly rises in a row.

A fall in London's stock is a change in where silver sits, not a measure of silver used up. Some of it may have gone to India, some to exchange-traded funds, which hold silver for investors and trade like shares, and some elsewhere. The LBMA does not say.

The vaults are well stocked but not full. They hold about 21% less than at their June 2021 peak. Metals Focus, a research firm, put the metal available outside those funds at about 267 Moz. Kitco reported the estimate alongside end-September vault data. That is nearly double the 136 Moz of London stock outside funds at the end of September 2025. Metals Focus and the Silver Institute called that a "record (reported) low", and it came weeks before London's October squeeze, when buyers struggled to find metal there. The two figures come from different reports and may not cover exactly the same metal. The 267 Moz figure also predates October's data, so the two cannot be combined to work out a new balance.

Funds may also have drawn on that metal. The iShares Silver Trust, which keeps most of its metal in London, added about 11 Moz from the end of September to November 10. If that metal came out of London's stock, the silver not held by funds fell by more than London's reported total did. That is my inference, because the LBMA does not split its figures by owner.

New York: Steady Through the Sell-Off

COMEX is the main US futures exchange, where traders agree a price today for silver delivered later. Its "registered" silver is metal with a warrant, a receipt that makes it ready for delivery. Registered stock stood at 101.63 Moz on November 9, on the exchange's own report. On November 18 it was about 101.2 Moz, on CME Group figures compiled by MetalCharts. The price fell hard over those nine days, and the deliverable metal hardly changed.

Open interest is the number of futures contracts still open. Counted in ounces, it came to about 5.7 for each registered ounce, the same ratio as a week earlier. Money managers, mostly hedge funds, held net bullish bets of 3,615 contracts on November 10. That is their bets on a rise minus their bets on a fall, and it is close to their lowest since February 2024.

So far fewer of these traders are betting on a rise than earlier in the year. The figure does not show how much forced selling is left, though. Large bets in both directions sit inside that small net number and cancel each other out.

Sources: LBMA, October and September 2026 vault data | LBMA, June 2021 record | CME Group, COMEX silver stocks, November 9 | MetalCharts, COMEX silver stocks from CME Group data, November 18 | CFTC, COMEX silver open interest and managed money, November 3 and 10 | Kitco, Metals Focus on London and positioning, October 29 | KNN India, citing Reuters, October 23 | India's Ministry of Commerce and Industry, September and October trade data, via Kitco and The Pamphlet | World Silver Survey 2026, Metals Focus and the Silver Institute

The open-interest ratio pairs the CFTC's November 10 figure with registered stock on November 18. The Kitco report carrying the 267 Moz figure does not give its date; it appears beside end-September vault data. The managed-money figures are longs minus shorts in the CFTC's disaggregated report. India's monthly trade release gives values, not tonnes.

 

India: The Buyer Came Back

India is the world's biggest silver consumer and imports most of what it uses. Dealers told Reuters that in late October the government issued permits to import about 6,500 tonnes over six months. That is about 209 Moz. It comes to roughly nine-tenths of India's imports in all of 2025, which Metals Focus and the Silver Institute put at 232.2 Moz.

A permit is a ceiling, not an order. When the permits were issued, Indian buyers were paying only 45 cents an ounce over official domestic prices. That points to a market that was not short of metal that week.

The first trade figures since then are firmer. India's commerce ministry put October silver imports at $1.91 billion. That is nearly three times September's figure. These are values, not volumes, and the price moved between the two months. October was still about 28% below October 2025, when India was buying heavily during the squeeze in London. November's figures, due in mid-December, will be the first full month under the new permits.

 

What This Means to Silver Investors

The stockpiles tell a different story from the price. A price that falls because there is too much silver around tends to leave metal sitting in vaults. In October, London's stock fell and India's imports rose. Into mid-November, New York's deliverable stock held. On one month of data, that is a small positive for the case that the world uses more silver than it produces.

It is not evidence of a shortage you can see yet. London is well stocked, nothing in New York showed strain, and India's buying came after months of curbs. Market reports blame the price fall largely on expectations of a December rate rise and a firmer dollar.

In their interim review on November 12, Metals Focus and the Silver Institute still forecast a sixth annual shortfall in a row, of about 35 Moz. That is smaller than the 46.3 Moz they expected in April. They also said that fund selling and the smaller shortfall have helped ease tightness this year in the physical market, where bars and coins change hands.

The next tests come quickly. November 30 is the first day buyers holding December contracts can be told their metal is ready for delivery. December is one of COMEX's main delivery months. data.title: Can Anthropic IPO Beat SpaceX To Become The World's Largest?
data.description:
Anthropic could price its shares above its proposed $70 to $78 range on Wednesday, putting the maker of Claude on course for one of the biggest stock market debuts ever.

Jay Ritter, director of the University of Florida’s IPO Initiative, told CNBC he expects the deal to “exceed SpaceX as the world’s largest IPO ever.”

At the $80 price he floated, however, Anthropic would still fall short on public proceeds under its current share count.

And for investors buying Anthropic stock as it goes live on Nasdaq, the bigger question is actually how much future profit that price already assumes.

What would it take to beat SpaceX?

At $80 a share, Anthropic’s planned sale of 825 million shares would generate $66 billion before fees, including proceeds going to existing shareholders.

That would rise to $75.9 billion if underwriters bought all the extra shares available to them.

SpaceX’s (SPCX) June debut brought in $75 billion initially and about $85.7 billion after its underwriters exercised their option.

On that like-for-like comparison, Anthropic would need a price above $90 per share with its extra allotment fully used, or a larger offering.

The separate $26 billion private placement with investors including Google (GOOGL) and Nvidia (NVDA) boosts the total raised alongside the listing.

But the IPO record counts money raised only through the public offering itself.

Ritter sees a first-day jump in Anthropic stock

Ritter said the shares were “very likely to jump” from his hypothetical $80 offer price.

But using his estimates of a $1.5 trillion valuation and $35.2 billion in trailing 12-month revenue, investors would be paying roughly 43 times annual sales.

In plain terms, that’s about $43 in company value for every dollar Anthropic generated in revenue over the previous year, before paying for the computing power and other costs needed to serve customers.

Ritter said that multiple could look conservative next to Palantir (PLTR) or SpaceX, but “a lot of things have to go right.”

One is keeping customers willing to pay premium prices as competing AI models improve.

Investors who bought SpaceX shares at the time of the IPO haven't done well, with the stock falling 10% since its debut.

What investors are buying beyond the growth story

Ritter also pointed to Anthropic’s public benefit structure as a sign that it takes AI safety seriously.

Its directors must weigh shareholders’ financial interests alongside the interests of people affected by the company and its stated public mission.

In practice, the board has room to back a safety decision even if it slows a product launch or raises costs.

Anthropic’s prospectus says its public benefit initiatives could reduce profitability per share.

The final offer price will settle how close Anthropic gets to SpaceX’s record. For anyone buying after trading starts, a first-day jump raises the bar.

The higher the entry price, the more profit Anthropic must eventually deliver to justify it.

data.title: Yen Threatens Key Level Ahead Of Inflation Data
data.description:
The USDJPY is just shy of the 160 level it touched last week, potentially triggering an intervention by Japanese authorities to arrest weakness in their currency. It’s a crucial juncture ahead of key data that will be decisive for the BOJ’s policy.

Investors are betting that Japan’s central bank won’t keep pace with a more hawkish Fed, which will widen the interest-rate gap between the currencies. The carry trade becomes increasingly interesting as the gap widens, but the potential for intervention by Japanese authorities could limit the upside. That is, unless there is a substantial shift in the underlying data that would encourage traders to challenge the financial authorities trying to slow the rise in the USDJPY.

The BOJ’s Inflation Problem

Japanese policymakers are concerned about their currency weakening too fast, as it would disrupt its trade-dependent economy. The main cause is that the BOJ maintains the lowest borrowing rates among the major currencies, making it profitable for traders to sell yen to buy other currencies. This is a growing problem as other central banks are poised to raise rates in December to address energy-induced inflationary pressures. (Australia’s RBA being a notable exception, but having already the highest rates among the majors.)

The way to deal with this problem is for the BOJ to raise rates along with its counterparts. But to justify such a move, there needs to be inflationary pressure, and Japan’s sluggish economy and high savings rates have kept inflation relatively low in the island nation. In fact, it was last reported practically on target, and if it continues to underperform, it could undermine the case for further rate hikes.

What the Market Is Looking For

On Friday, Japan will report its October CPI data, and it is expected to show headline CPI at 2.0%, down from 2.1% a month earlier. The slight downward variation is expected to be attributed to easing energy prices. The so-called “core core” rate (excluding energy and food costs, equivalent to other countries’ “core”) is projected to remain unchanged at 2.4%.

With the core rate above target, the BOJ has an excuse to pursue or at least signal a hawkish stance. So, if the core rate were to decline, it could embolden the market to weaken the yen. Likewise, if the headline inflation rate falls substantially below target, it could shake the BOJ’s resolve to raise rates.

What Are the Odds of a BOJ Hike?

At the moment, the market is pricing in an 86% chance of a December BOJ rate hike, allowing it to keep pace with the Fed and ECB, both of which are also expected to raise rates at the same time. If that dynamic persists, it would be easier for Japanese authorities to keep a lid on the USDJPY.

Hotter-than-expected inflation would raise the odds of a rate hike, but the market is already fairly confident in one, reducing the potential impact. Since the recent move higher in USDJPY is mostly due to the dollar, it’s unlikely the currency pair will reverse substantially on Japanese data. This means the potential for a bigger surprise is to the upside (weaker yen).

The speed of that reversal caught my attention, particularly because it illustrates something I’ve spent much of my career studying: how fear influences stock prices and what happens when that fear begins to fade.

The immediate concern was artificial intelligence. Following the midterm elections, questions emerged about whether additional restrictions on data center development could slow the industry’s expansion. Companies involved in building AI infrastructure were particularly vulnerable because their growth expectations depend on continued spending.

There is a financial reason these concerns can produce such dramatic price movements: Building AI infrastructure requires enormous upfront investments in chips, electricity, cooling systems, and data centers. Much of the expected financial return will come years from now. Anything that threatens future revenue growth or increases financing costs can significantly affect how these companies are valued today.

By contrast however, an encouraging economic report emerged shortly after the selloff.

On November 6, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that employers added 165,000 jobs in October, compared with an average monthly gain of just 48,000 over the previous year. The unemployment rate declined to 4.1%, and employment estimates for August and September were revised upward by a combined 84,000 jobs.

Those figures suggest the labor market remains stronger than recent hiring trends had indicated. However, economic strength creates another consideration for the stock market.

The Federal Reserve is balancing employment conditions against inflation. Stronger hiring can reduce the urgency to lower interest rates, particularly if inflation remains elevated. Higher borrowing costs can weigh on corporate earnings and make future profits less valuable in today’s dollars.

For technology companies already facing questions about expensive expansion plans, that combination creates additional uncertainty.

But uncertainty and fear are not the same thing, and fear can move stock prices well beyond what the underlying economic information might justify.

That relationship has been the focus of my research for years.

I developed my Income Trader Volatility indicator to identify periods when fear reaches unusually elevated levels and begins to reverse. My research, which earned the Charles H. Dow Award in 2015, examined historical market data from 1999 through 2014 and found that weekly signals produced stronger results than daily signals.

My research reinforced an important lesson about volatility. A sharp market decline is not automatically a buying opportunity. Prices can continue falling even after a substantial selloff, and some declines reflect genuine deterioration in business conditions.

What interests me is the change in volatility after fear has intensified.

The CBOE Volatility Index, or VIX, provides one way to observe that behavior. It measures expected volatility in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days using options prices. During periods of uncertainty, demand for protection can increase, driving the VIX higher. When that demand subsides, volatility can retreat quickly, even before the broader economic questions have been resolved.

My indicator takes that concept further by looking for specific conditions associated with extremes in fear and subsequent changes in market behavior. The recent market decline provides a useful example of why I approach trading this way.

We cannot know whether concerns about AI spending will lead to a prolonged correction, or whether the recent decline will prove temporary. We also cannot know exactly how the Federal Reserve will respond to the next inflation report.

Fortunately, identifying potential trades does not require predicting either outcome.

Market conditions will continue to change as new economic data, corporate earnings, and policy decisions shape expectations. Some developments will justify changes in stock prices, while others may produce temporary reactions driven by fear. My indicator helps me identify opportunities when volatility reaches extremes and begins to reverse, allowing me to make trading decisions based on measurable market conditions, rather than predictions about what might happen next.

data.title: Indian Rupee Advances As Appeal Of India's Non-AI Growth Story Remains Strong
data.description:
The Indian Rupee (INR) bounces back against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday after a brief pause the previous day. As of writing, the USD/INR pair is down 0.13% to near 93.34 despite the US Dollar Index (DXY) strengthening further.

The US Dollar extends its rally due to fears of a series of interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve (Fed) in the near term. During the day, the US Dollar Index (DXY), which gauges the Greenback’s value against six major currencies, hits a fresh 19-month high near 104.00.

What to expect From Fed in near term?

According to the CME FedWatch Tool, the Fed is almost certain to deliver interest rate hikes of 25 basis points (bps) at the December and January policy meetings. The tool shows an almost 50% chance of another rate hike in March 2027.

The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes of the October policy meeting also showed on Wednesday that policymakers have explicitly supported further interest rate hikes, while warning that “inflation may be more persistent than anticipated”.

The minutes also showed that a couple of policymakers warned of a bigger interest rate hike in the December meeting if inflation data continues to remain negative.

FIIs buying and lower oil prices to keep INR’s downside limited

Analysts at Societe Generale highlight the Indian Rupee as “the surprise star performer in EMs this month,” noting that the move has been “powered by FPI inflows” as investors broaden market bets beyond “AI-themed markets like South Korea and Taiwan.” They add that sentiment has also been supported by “optimism over Iran truce following US midterm election that has deflated Brent towards $90/b,” reinforcing the constructive backdrop for INR.

So far in November, Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) have remained net buyers in all full-length trading days and have increased their stake worth Rs. 94,229.56 crore.

Meanwhile, lower oil prices due to eased fears of energy supply risks from the Middle East are also expected to support the INR’s downside. As of writing, the MCX Crude Oil contract expiring on December 18 is up 0.78% to near Rs. 7,709, but is close to its 11-week low of Rs. 7,850.

USD/INR Technical Analysis

In the daily chart, USD/INR trades at 93.34, maintaining a bearish near-term tone as it holds below the 20-period exponential moving average (EMA) at 94.23. The pair remains pressured by this overhead dynamic resistance, while the Relative Strength Index (RSI) at 28.23 sits in oversold territory, hinting that while downside momentum is stretched, sellers still dominate the short-term structure.

On the topside, the immediate level to watch is the 20-period EMA resistance at 94.23, which would need to be reclaimed to ease the current bearish bias and open room for a corrective bounce. On the downside, the November 18 low at 93.25 is the immediate support; below that the 93.00 level would act as key cushion.

data.title: Revolut Tokenized Funds: 4 Private-Market Funds Head On-Chain. What Retail Investors Should Know
data.description:
Revolut chair Martin Gilbert said on Tuesday, November 17, that the fintech plans to launch four tokenized funds, letting its customers buy small slices of private-market investments on a blockchain. He spoke at Solana’s Breakpoint conference in London.

The funds would hold assets such as private equity, which normally can’t be sold quickly, and use a blockchain to cut them into what Gilbert called “marketable sizes.”

Revolut has more than 80 million customers, so tokenized funds in its app could reach far more everyday savers than most tokenization projects do today. But the timing is awkward. We tracked the share prices of the four firms that already manage Revolut’s private-market funds. All four are down this year, by a median of 28%, while the S&P 500 is up 7%.

So can tokenized funds fix the problem Gilbert describes, getting money out of assets that are hard to sell?

Revolut Tokenized Funds: Announced, but Few Details Yet

Gilbert framed the plan around one problem: getting money back out. “In this world, there is liquidity until there is no liquidity,” he said. “If you can help people get liquidity in illiquid assets, you’re going to solve a lot of problems for a lot of people.”

Liquidity here means being able to sell quickly at a fair price. Private equity funds usually lock money up for years. Splitting a fund into tokens on a blockchain could, in theory, let investors trade those tokens with each other instead of waiting for the fund to pay them out.

Revolut has not shared much beyond that:

  • Not disclosed: the fund names, managers, strategies, fees, legal structure and launch date.

  • Blockchain: not named. Gilbert spoke at a Solana event, but Revolut hasn’t confirmed which network the funds will use.

  • Who can buy: not stated. Revolut’s current private-market funds are open only to eligible customers in Europe.

The plan builds on a product Revolut launched on July 27. Its Private Markets section lets eligible European customers invest from €1 in funds run by Apollo, Ares, Hamilton Lane and Partners Group. Those funds use the EU’s ELTIF 2.0 rules, a framework that lets retail investors buy long-term funds. Subscriptions are generally monthly and redemptions quarterly. Holders can’t move them to another broker or sell them to other investors.

Private Markets Managers Are Down 28% This Year

The four managers Revolut picked are some of the biggest names in private markets. Their share prices show how investors feel about the business right now.

  • Revolut’s partners: Apollo is down 19% since the end of 2025, Ares 21%, Partners Group 35% and Hamilton Lane 35%.

  • The wider group: Blackstone, the largest private-markets firm, is down 25%, and KKR 26%.

  • The market: the S&P 500 is up 7% over the same period.

  • Since Revolut’s launch: from July 27 to now, Apollo and Partners Group fell about 6%, while Ares and Hamilton Lane were roughly flat.

Part of the worry is exactly the liquidity Gilbert talked about. In June, Partners Group capped withdrawals from an $8.6 billion fund after investors asked for 9.8% of its assets back, nearly double its 5% limit, Bloomberg reported. Apollo and Ares have also limited redemptions on some funds that promise investors regular access to their money.

That’s the case for tokenized funds, and also its limit. A token can make a fund easier to trade, but only if someone wants to buy it. When many holders want out at once, a token changes how a share is sold, not whether a buyer shows up.

Tokenized Funds Already Exist, Mostly for Professionals

Revolut wouldn’t be first. Apollo and Hamilton Lane already offer tokenized credit funds through Securitize, a company that issues fund shares as tokens on blockchains. Those products are mostly sold to institutions and wealthy investors with high minimums.

There is even a token linked to Revolut itself, though Revolut has nothing to do with it. $CREV, issued by Swiss firm Colb Finance on BNB Chain, tracks the value of Revolut shares before any stock market listing. It launched on May 28 with a $25,000 minimum for professional investors, and holders get price exposure only, with no voting rights. Revolut has not announced a date for listing its own shares.

What Revolut could change is scale. Moving funds like these into an app with 80 million users, at small ticket sizes, would test whether tokenized funds can work for ordinary savers.

data.title: The Final Dollar Spike Before The Crack-Up Boom
data.description:
IT IS DIFFERENT THIS TIME. IT’S A FIRST AS WELL.

To date, we have 4000+ years of recorded commerce with banking and interest rates, 300+ years of experimentation with some form of central banking/reserve currencies, and more than 50 years of an unhinged fiat monetary system. But this is the first time in human history that we are going to experience the follow-on effects of the loosening part of a credit cycle (under a worldwide fiat currency system) that started bottoming earlier this decade, when the 30-year Treasury rate hit a nadir of 0.7% in 2020.

Even after the start in 1971 of the fiat system, the first decade and a half was really dealing with the effects of credit loosening that happened during the Gold Exchange Standard of the 1960s, with the advent of Guns AND Butter, i.e., the Vietnam War, as well as the Great Society program that included the War on Poverty, Medicare, and Medicaid. It was not until the Maestro, Alan Greenspan, came along that the world embarked on a unidirectional experiment with easy money (as evidenced by falling 30-year Treasury rates and rising national debt).

With no real-world examples of what lies ahead, how then do we extrapolate it? Fortunately, we are in the good hands of Von Mises and Rothbard’s “Austrian Business Cycle Theory”, or, as it is more commonly referred to, the “Boom-Bust Cycles of Monetary Inflation”.  Besides, there is extensive evidence that the first two smaller boom-bust cycles, as explained below and leading up to today’s crescendo, have indeed panned out as forecasted in ABCT.

1990 to 2022 – THE GREAT MONETARY EASING CYCLE WITHOUT A PAYBACK

A short summary of how the Business Cycle works is given below

  1. The lowering of interest rates by the US Fed results in malinvestments (leading to supply in excess of demand, as would be mandated by genuine savings) being made. These investments would eventually have to be liquidated, resulting in the bust.

    • Good examples of the malinvestments would be the internet infrastructure created around the year 2000 as part of Nasdaq’s Irrational Exuberance Another good example of excess supply is the 2008 housing bubble.

  2. The malinvestments are the result of an excess supply of money and credit directed towards specific industries/assets. This credit eventually spills over into consumer prices, forcing the Federal Reserve to hike rates. This intermediary, temporary tightening (within the overall easing of the 30-year easing cycle from 1990) brings about the bust and eventually leads to a recession.

  3. If the recession is allowed to run its course without any fiscal and monetary interventions, then the malinvestments of the prior period are cleared by the markets and the economy restarts on a more balanced foundation. But invariably, governments intervene, prolonging and worsening the structural imbalances.

  4. The cycle of boom-bust keeps repeating till we reach the point that Mises referred to as the “Crack Up Boom,” i.e., hyperinflation. Any easing attempted at this point would result in a rapid decline in the currency’s purchasing power.

  5. Some facets of the boom-bust cycle are given below for a better understanding.

    • The later cycles of monetary easing need increasingly greater stimulus to produce the desired effects. For example, an interest rate of 3% for a couple of years led to the NASDAQ 2000 bubble. The easing after the dotcom bust required a 1% interest rate to stimulate the economy. The easing required after the GFC in 2008 was, of course, on a logarithmic scale higher than the previous round. With nearly 15 years of ZIRP coupled with Quantitative easing, and a near 10-fold increase in the US Fed Balance sheet, the monetary stimulus required to bring about a semblance of stability was unprecedented.

    • The extent of the bust or the depth of the recession is proportional to the monetary stimulus that led to the artificial boom. It stands to reason that the malinvestments that need to be liquidated are indeed a function of the stimulus applied. The recession of 2000, after the dotcom crash, was indeed bigger than those of the 1980s and 1990s, but pales in comparison to the Great Financial Crisis of 2008.

Which brings us to the here and now. What type of recession/depression are we looking at ahead when the current malinvestments have to be liquidated? We will get to that in a while, after comparing the prior bubbles with the current ones.

 

A COMPARISON OF BUBBLES

A few short comments on the above comparison would be helpful before we proceed further.

  1. The size of current bubbles is much larger as compared to the previous cycle bubbles. This follows from the fact that the size of the economic stimulus has been much greater, leading to greater levels of malinvestments.

  2. Perhaps more than the size/scale of bubbles, it is the changing credit conditions that will cause much greater disruptions to the markets on account of the bubbles bursting.

  3. The current bubbles are winding down under conditions of tightening credit, increasing price inflation, increasing 30-year Treasury rates, and an economy on the verge of a depression rather than a severe recession.

  4. The traditional fiscal/monetary policy tools (rate cuts, QEs, etc.) used to handle the previous cycle’s bubbles bursting would be ineffective. Indeed, would probably be very counterproductive, leading to a swift destruction of the purchasing power of the US Dollar.

  5. An economic depression, with cumulative GDP contraction in excess of 25%, is the best-case scenario for the US. In all probability, this would be accompanied by very high price inflation, but is not outright Hyperinflation.


HOW DID THE US EVEN END UP HERE? WHAT WENT WRONG AND WHERE?

We can start the blame game with Greenspan, and it would indeed be very appropriate to do so. Given his understanding of Austrian economics, as he wrote so eloquently in “Gold and Economic Freedom”, Greenspan would have known that the state today would be the endgame. The Road of Monetary Easing provides no easy U-turns.

But why step on his grave when we have equally culpable individuals around us? If Gold and Economic Freedom were an intellectual masterpiece, the Courage to Act is its Antithesis. Bernanke often quotes, and supposedly draws inspiration from, Walter Bagehot’s “Lombard Street: A Description of the Money Market”.

Most Austrian economists despise the idea of a central bank and believe its functions fundamentally violate individual property rights. But given the reality of existence, I suspect most would agree with Bagehot’s proposal for a central bank’s role in a crisis: “lend freely against good collateral at a high rate of interest.”

Whatever happens in the months ahead is a direct outcome of Greenspan’s initial monetary easing actions, carried on in increasing spades by every successive Fed Bank Chair without exception. This is the result of more than 30 years of loose monetary policy, artificially low interest rates, and an unhinged US Federal Government Spending plan through the decades.

Courage for a Central Banker is to keep real interest rates high in the face of political opposition. When price inflation in the US was around 13% during 1980-81, Volcker hiked the Fed funds rates to more than 20%, offering a real yield of nearly 8%. What Bernanke did at the helm was keep real interest rates negative throughout his tenure. This is not courage. A more appropriate title for his book Courage to Act would be A Sellout to the Banking Cartel.

 

THE US DOLLAR’s ENDGAME

While it’s important to understand why the CRB Bubble has been replaced by a bubble in US Bonds today, the explanation would have to be extensive and perhaps beyond the interests of most readers. An easier way would be to just look at data – the relative valuation of Commodities vis-à-vis financial assets.

On a relative basis, Commodities today, and despite the CRB index nearly quadrupling over the last 6 years, remains at levels below those of 1970 and 2000 – the two previous bear market bottoms in the space of commodities.

I don’t have a crystal ball for when precisely the HB2.0 and AI bubbles will burst. Or as to what event would trigger the same. At least on valuations, we are well below the peak in median housing prices. The SpaceX post-IPO sugar rush might well have been the peak of the AI bubble.

In the recent sell-offs, the dollar has strengthened against other currencies and gold. This is a typical market reaction when market players deleverage existing speculative positions (AI trades, housing-related investment positions) and their safe trades (gold and commodities). Few realize that swapping gold for dollars at this point is perhaps the worst strategic swap one can make given the setup. Gold is well on its way as the rightful choice as the Numero Uno Neutral Reserve Asset, while the US Dollar is on the verge of a Crack Up Boom and possibly becoming confetti. 

What is certain is that when the bubbles burst, the Fed would have no option but to double down on QEs. Especially with the market constraint on how low interest rates can be pushed, given prevailing price inflation. In the reflation trade, even with very conservative projections, the bull market ahead in commodities is going to be one for the record books.

data.title: Physical Gold: The Ultimate Form Of Asset Ownership
data.description:
Whatever asset we hold, whether financial or real, the question of ownership security always arises. In the event of a crisis, an attack, fraud or an unforeseen event, do I still retain full ownership of my assets and the freedom to dispose of them as I see fit? When we delve deeper into this question, we enter murky territory.

Recent events have revealed new threats. Bitcoin (BTC.X) holders believed they could protect themselves by storing their assets on hardware wallets (Ledger, Trezor or others), thereby shielding themselves from the potential collapse of the platform on which they had purchased them (recall the collapse of FTX in 2022). Unfortunately, data breaches have made them targets of criminal networks, and many have fallen victim to violent home invasions. Another form of theft has recently emerged: on October 9, it was revealed that several Ledger hardware wallets sold in Asia had been compromised. Malicious components had been implanted in the devices, allowing funds to be siphoned off. The local authorised reseller (CryptoBilis), which had recently been acquired, is suspected of involvement, but is this an isolated case? Last summer, another hardware wallet manufacturer, Coldcard, was generating recovery phrases (used in the event of a lost device) through a process that was insufficiently random, allowing AI to reconstruct these phrases using limited information about the device. Tens of millions of dollars were stolen.

Should we therefore turn back to the major cryptocurrency exchanges? Not really. On October 29, Binance, the largest of these platforms, fell victim to the biggest hack in history, with $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrencies stolen. Customers suffered no losses, but the threat remains.

Should we ultimately turn to traditional banks? Doing so would mean forgetting the warning of the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis, during which the collapse of Lehman Brothers nearly triggered a chain reaction of bank failures. Other institutions have since failed, including Silicon Valley Bank in March 2023, which was, after all, the 16th-largest bank in the United States. Why did it fail? Faced with withdrawal requests from its customers, the bank was forced to sell its holdings of US Treasury securities. However, these securities had been acquired during a period of low interest rates. As rates rose, their market value fell, leaving the institution unable to meet its obligations.

This situation can now be found, to varying degrees, across Western banks: their balance sheets are filled with sovereign bonds acquired several years ago, when interest rates were low. A forced sale in an environment where interest rates stand at 5% or higher could result in substantial losses! With public debt soaring around the world, a crisis in the sovereign debt market would quickly spread to the banking sector. Holders of life insurance policies, whose funds are largely invested in sovereign debt securities, would also be directly affected.

Like cryptocurrency exchanges, banks are exposed to the risk of cyberattacks. On November 5, a French bank, Crédit Mutuel, reportedly suffered a theft of around €100 million following a sophisticated cyberattack. Customers were not affected, but such incidents could become increasingly common in the future…

When it comes to equities, ownership rights appear to be more secure, but they generally depend on banks or platforms that may themselves fail. Except in certain arrangements, investors do not hold their securities directly, but through what is known as a “trusted third party”, with all the risks that entails.

Surely real estate remains an option? Certainly, but is it a financial asset in the strict sense of the term? In the case of one's primary residence, the answer is no: you cannot sell just a portion of it, only sell it in its entirety or mortgage it. Owning several properties comes closer to holding an investment asset, but the time required to sell them is considerably longer than for the assets discussed above. Nevertheless, real estate ownership does offer a solid degree of security.

Physical gold stored outside the banking system, with full ownership and held in one's own name, offers one of the safest forms of asset ownership. Storing gold at home exposes owners to significant risks and is therefore best avoided. It is also essential to verify the provenance and authenticity of gold bars to eliminate the risk of counterfeiting using tungsten, whose density is close to that of gold. As for paper gold, it rests on a promise and is therefore best avoided. Ultimately, the non-digital nature of the yellow metal proves to be an advantage! Its unique characteristics make gold an indispensable asset.

data.title: EUR/USD Remains Under Selling Pressure As Dollar Strength Persists
data.description:
Speculators who have been convinced now is the time to take advantage of the negative trend in the EUR/USD because they feel the currency pair has been oversold, were reminded yet again why it is unsafe to jump ahead of the crowd. The EUR/USD continues to create velocity which is an exceptionally good thing for some day traders – when they are on the correct side of price momentum. The EUR/USD promises to remain a highlight reel in Forex in the short and near-term this as financial institutions are tested regarding their sentiment, along with retail traders going along for the ride.

Fed Rate Expectations and Market Anxiety Weigh on EUR/USD

As if the negative momentum in the EUR/USD has not been enough over the last few weeks, the past two days have dealt another blow to those hoping for a sudden reversal upwards to be demonstrated in a sustained manner. The addition of more rhetoric coming from a Federal Reserve official saying the U.S central bank should be more aggressive regarding interest rate hikes helped create USD centric strength in the broad Forex market that some financial institutions were clearly not anticipating.

The EUR/USD is correlating to the broad market which remains nervous. U.S Treasury yields remain inflated. All of these ingredients into the EUR/USD is creating a segment of Forex speculators who are anxious and likely waiting for further impetus. Volatility in the near-term is a basic assumption that is widespread.

EUR/USD Tests Recent Lows as Safe-Haven Dollar Demand Grows

The EUR/USD hit lows around the 1.09525 mark briefly yesterday, as of this writing the currency pair is near 1.09720 with fast price action prevalent. Speculators hoping to take advantage of the velocity in the currency pair need to be watching technical charts, but they also need to understand nervous sentiment is high. Global equities remain fragile and this is causing some investors to seek safe havens and this is causing a rather strong steady shift into the USD.

However, there is plenty of reasons to believe something else is going to happen in the broad marketplace which could set off additional fireworks. Unfortunately for retail traders if nervous emotions grow this will mean Forex could be a focal point and cause more mayhem. While it is logical to believe a reversal will occur in the EUR/USD that is noteworthy, the problem for all traders – big and small – is betting correctly on timeframes. Because trying to guess when trajectories are going to change directions is at best dangerous, retail traders will be safer using a conservative approach with the EUR/USD as it struggles and challenges lows.

Why Oversold Conditions May Not Signal a EUR/USD Reversal

There are dynamics in the broad markets which are likely to cause a collision of outlooks. WTI Crude Oil prices have been declining. If energy prices start to become cheaper this will cause inflation to lessen, yet central bankers are not known to be quick regarding their monetary policy. The fact they may remain ultra-cautious may continue to create interest rate hawks which could weigh down the EUR/USD in the meantime, that is until a sea change of attitudes occurs. The EUR/USD downside price action has been very strong. At some point support levels and pure oversold notions are bound to become strong, but when that is going to prove it is working remains an open question. Those looking for more downside in the EUR/USD near-term cannot be faulted, but they need to also be cautious.

Persistent Selling Pressure Challenges the Case for a Euro Recovery

If bullish traders have survived the past few days and are still holding onto a stubborn belief the EUR/USD is oversold they cannot be blamed. However, the price velocity lower in the EUR/USD should be a reminder the currency pair has seen lower values before. There is no reason to doubt the EUR/USD can move to further depths that test the patience of EUR backers. Looking for momentum to suddenly shift upwards in a strong manner remains unlikely. Those looking for upside need to be careful with their wagers.

What Could Change the EUR/USD Outlook as Volatility Persists?

Volatility in the EUR/USD remains problematic for those who carry pro-EUR bias. The moves lower in the currency pair the past handful of weeks has been rather constant. Yes, reversals upwards intraday are definitely part of the trading landscape, but speculators need to remain careful. Feeling uneasy about the current EUR/USD is likely a good survival instinct protecting you from being too ambitious.

data.title: Canadian Dollar Moves Little As Surging Oil Prices Offset Stronger US Dollar
data.description:
USD/CAD pulls back after hitting a fresh 19-month high of 1.4357 during earlier hours, remaining flat around 1.4330 during European hours on Thursday. The pair could regain ground as the US Dollar (USD) holds onto its gains, supported by increasingly hawkish signals from the Federal Reserve (Fed).

Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) Meeting Minutes released on Wednesday revealed that while policymakers opted for a temporary hold in October to gather more economic data, they agreed on the necessity of further interest rate hikes to tame inflation. Although most officials anticipate additional increases, a few even floated the possibility of a 50-basis-point hike if upcoming inflation figures disappoint.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller stated that the FOMC should consider a half-point increase in December, while John Williams and Alberto Musalem also indicated that tighter policy may be warranted. Consequently, the CME FedWatch tool shows markets pricing in a nearly 93% probability of a 25-basis-point hike next month, alongside a greater than 7% chance of a 50-basis-point move.

On the other hand, upside potential for the USD/CAD pair may be capped if rising oil prices bolster the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD). West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude is holding above $82.00 per barrel as escalating geopolitical supply risks outweigh expectations of a market surplus.

In the Middle East, Iranian media reported on Wednesday that mines disabled three oil tankers east of the Strait of Hormuz, followed by Houthi missile attacks toward Riyadh on Thursday that Saudi Civil Defense said no longer pose a threat. Simultaneously, Reuters reported that Ukrainian drone strikes have cut Russian oil refineries' combined crude processing volumes by 45% since late October.

Looking ahead, broader oil market sentiment remains caught between diplomatic hopes and inventory data. Traders are closely awaiting a trilateral summit between the leaders of the US, China, and Russia for signs of a negotiated resolution to both the US-Iran conflict and the war in Ukraine, which continue to disrupt global energy supplies.

data.title: Japanese Yen Declines On Hawkish Fed Minutes
data.description:
The USD/JPY pair gathers strength to near 159.50 during the early European trading hours on Thursday. Federal Reserve meeting minutes and hawkish comments from a Fed official pointed to further interest ‌rate hikes, boosting the US Dollar (USD) against the Japanese Yen (JPY). Traders remain on high alert for currency intervention from Japanese authorities.

Federal Reserve (Fed) meeting minutes released Wednesday indicated officials expressed confidence in October that further interest rate increases will be needed to curb inflation, though they decided to hold off while gathering more data.

The statement also showed two policymakers said a hike of “more than 25 basis points” could be warranted in December if incoming inflation data proved unfavorable.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller reiterated his belief that the central bank should consider a half-point hike in December. Meanwhile, Fed officials John Williams and Alberto Musalem also signaled further rate hikes may be needed to curb inflation.

According to a majority of economists in a Reuters ‌poll, the Bank of Japan (BoJ) will raise interest rates for the third time this year at its December meeting and follow up with another by end-March as the central bank remains focused on inflation and a weak currency.

On Thursday, BoJ Governor Kazuo Ueda said that underlying inflation roughly aligns with the price target. Ueda added that the central bank plans to continue raising interest rates as monetary conditions remain accommodative. His comments followed news that Japan's core consumer inflation exceeded the 2% target for the first time in nine months in September.

"Because of the US-Japan interest rate gap, the yen is more likely to weaken...If the ‌BOJ does not hike in December, the yen could weaken further, which could add to upward pressure on prices," said Kei Fujimoto, senior economist at Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management.

USD/JPY seen consolidating as UOB shifts to range-trading stance

Strategists at UOB Group note that recent price action in USD/JPY has been more subdued than anticipated. They recall that yesterday they had indicated the Dollar “could rebound further,” while cautioning that “it should stay within a range of 159.20/159.80.” Instead, the pair “traded sideways between 159.11 and 159.65 before closing marginally lower by 0.01% at 159.33.” In the near term, they expect “further sideways-trading” to dominate, “probably between 159.15 and 159.70.”

On a 1–3 week horizon, UOB reiterates that it “revised our view from positive to neutral yesterday (18 Nov, spot at 159.50)” and now judges that “upward pressure has eased, and USD has likely entered a range-trading phase between 158.60 and 160.15.” The bank adds that “there is no change in our view,” underscoring its conviction that USD/JPY is set to remain confined within this broader consolidation band for the time being.

Ueda flags inflation overshoot risks as BoJ leans toward further tightening

FXS Speechtracker’s 8/10 score versus the 7.5/10 historic average signals a modestly more hawkish tone, with Governor Ueda emphasizing that underlying inflation is roughly at target and warning that inflation could exceed the Bank of Japan’s objective. The commitment to continue raising interest rates while financial conditions remain loose, alongside simulations showing accelerated ETF sales will not severely damage BoJ finances, reinforces a gradual tightening bias even as real rates in the short end stay low and support activity.

Ueda’s focus on anchoring core inflation near 2% and highlighting that a weak Yen and rising crude prices could push inflation higher underscores concern about an inflation overshoot, especially as firms pass on costs more actively. At the same time, the acknowledgment that consumption has softened but should resume a moderate rise as wages increase, and that the pace and timing of rate hikes will depend on how baseline projections and risks evolve, points to a data-dependent but clearly hawkish tilt that leaves the Yen sensitive to upside inflation surprises and further rate hike signals.

Technical Analysis: USD/JPY retains a positive tone above the 100-day SMA

In the daily chart, USD/JPY holds above the 100-day moving average (MA) and the Bollinger middle band, keeping the near-term bias bullish as price grinds higher within the upper half of the volatility envelope.
